title: Open a children's bike's V-brake to free the front wheel: squeeze the sprung arms and lift the noodle out
keywords: squeeze and release with two hands
instruction: Open the bike's front brake so that the front wheel can be taken out.
context: Anyone who has fixed a flat on a bike with rim brakes has done this first: a V-brake's pads hug the rim closer than the tyre is wide, so the brake must be opened before the wheel comes out. Park Tool's wheel removal guide: "Squeeze linear-pull calipers together and disconnect cable 'noodle' from linkage"; a bike maker's help page: "If you squeeze the brake arms together, you can pull the noodle out of the black or silver tab that it is hooked into." The two arms are sprung apart and the cable holds them, so the noodle's end is pressed into its holder. One hand must keep both arms squeezed (pads on the rim, about 9 N each) to slacken the cable while the other draws the curved noodle back and lifts it out; pulled alone it does not come out (the brake just swings as one), and the arms snap back as soon as the squeeze is let go. Freed, they spring wide open.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. A 14-inch children's bike (steel frame, painted blue, fixed in place) stands upright facing the robot, its rear wheel in a slot-type floor stand at the table's far edge: wheelbase 53 cm, front axle at x 21.7, y 0, 17.2 up, rear axle at x 74.7; 14 x 1.75 tyres (34.3 cm across, 4.4 cm wide) on ISO 254 rims; handlebar 50 cm wide, grips 59 cm up at x 37; saddle top 53 cm up at x 60. Fork leaning back 20 degrees. Front V-brake (black aluminium arms, 60 g each): pivots on the fork 8 cm apart, 8.8 cm below the cable along the fork; pads 3 mm off the rim; each arm sprung outward (7 N at the cable). The cable crosses 1.1 cm above the tyre, centre at x 26, y 0, 34.8 up; anchor bolt on the arm at y +3.6. On the bike's left arm (y -3.6) a link holds the end of the noodle (90-degree aluminium tube 6 mm across, 8 mm ferrule seated 4 mm deep, end at y -1.0), which rises at y -2.8 to 41.9 up, with a rubber boot and the housing to the left lever. Both arms start at the ready pose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step from the brake arms' angles and the noodle's pose in the link's frame. 0 for the rest of the run if the noodle is forced up out of its cup (risen 2.5 mm while its end is still 3 mm or more inside: the link bends). Otherwise the best stage reached: 0.25 the noodle's end 4.5 mm or more back from its seat (clear of the cup); 0.5 the noodle lifted out of the link (its end 12 mm or more above the cup's middle). At the moment: 0.75 the noodle out and the pads 46 mm or more apart (the 44 mm tyre passes between them). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): that, both grippers' centres 5 cm or more from the noodle and the arms' tops, the noodle and arms still (under 2 mm and 0.5 degrees in 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the noodle out of its holder, seen on the video; a ruler between the pads, or the wheel dropped out between them; a bent link scores 0.
reset_notes: Squeeze the arms together, seat the noodle's end back in the link's holder (as when refitting the wheel) and let the arms go; check the pads sit about 3 mm off the rim each side and the bike stands in its stand at the marked spot. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics. The bike and wheel are fixed; each brake arm turns on its pivot with a spring (0.8 N m/rad, estimate) and stops (pad on the rim 4.6 deg in, 18 deg out); pads, rim and fork legs do not collide. The bare inner cable is a joint that only pulls: the noodle can come toward the anchor bolt (slack) but not farther than its seated distance. The housing is not modelled: the noodle stays where it is put (no gravity, damped) and turns freely about the cable's cross axis.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went to the front fork's lower leg by the hub, below the brake, and never touched the brake arms or the noodle; then both arms folded back and stayed there); demo: 1.0
